learning_outcomes.text: Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of energy generation, energy conversion, energy storage, and energy transport topics. The focus is on technologies that will enable a sustainable, environmentally, and socially compatible energy supply in the future.
Analyze energy conversion and transport chains.
Select and design suitable energy storage systems (especially battery systems, thermal storage, compressed air storage, power-to-gas plants).
Evaluate and design regenerative energy systems (especially wind power, solar thermal, and photovoltaic systems).
Evaluate and design decentralized energy supply systems (especially combined heat and power plants).
Assess the economic viability of various energy conversion systems.
Analyze and evaluate measures for efficiency enhancement and pollutant reduction in gas engines.
Collaborate in pairs on small projects, such as designing regenerative energy systems, and learn about group dynamic processes in solving technical problems.
Apply theoretical foundations practically through the design of energy systems using modern design tools or by programming design tools.
Investigate processes in a combined heat and power plant using appropriate measurement technology.

syllabus_topics: Most important renewable energy systems (wind power, photovoltaics, and solar thermal)
Most important energy storage systems (battery storage, thermal storage, compressed air storage, and power-to-gas)
Basic design and constructive features of these technologies
Evaluation of sites for suitability for a wind power, photovoltaic, or solar thermal plant
Design of wind power, photovoltaic, and solar thermal plants
Application of developed equations and design regulations using a programming language
Calculation and evaluation of system economic viability
Design and evaluation of electrochemical, mechanical, and thermal energy storage systems
Fossil energy resources and their range
Properties of transmission grids for electricity, gas, and liquid fuels
Time dependence of energy consumption (load profiles)
Impacts of electromobility and renewable energy systems
Introduction to combined heat and power (and cooling) (CHPC)
Large-scale power plants and possibilities for heat extraction
Gas turbines, Stirling and steam engines
Fuels for CHPC (natural gas, biogas, landfill gas, sewage gas, PtG, hydrogen, etc.)
Optimization of gas engines regarding efficiency and emissions
Coupling of CHPC with adsorption and absorption refrigeration systems
Integration of CHPC into the energy infrastructure
Experiments on combined heat and power plants at the Institute for Refrigeration, Air Conditioning and Environmental Engineering
assessment_rules: The examination format (written or oral) will be determined by the lecturer at the beginning of the course.
